reviews.text: Good concept BAD execution Let me explain. My gripes come from the combat. even games like Z-Crew got it right and had BOTH a sprint and a dodge button for getting out of those really sticky situations or creating some distance. There is no sprint button, only a roll with a cool down, this will FRUSTRATE you to no end, as the reload is to long to properly reload before an enemy runs up to you, locking you into an endless roll to avoid the insanely stupidly overly fast zombies. this game is NOT optimized for solo play, and you as a solo player will be swarmed and killed by enemies in to an endless cycle of death that isn't fun. you don't have the ammo count sprint or skills to properly fighting the enemies the game throws at you as a solo player. enemies have WAY to much health compared to the ammo you carry. are you trying to create resident evil or a top down twin stick shooter because you need to decide! Every single action movement and thing you do in this game is SLUGGISH and just frustrating while the zombies can sprint like i am legend! Also you built the game with four playable characters, but lock to three in a party? why just why? this is a small gripe but really gender locked classes are kinda lame I love the style and character that went into these guys, but it would be cool to see both a male and female version of each class. since the game lacks any character customization at all. The game has potential but it needs some love.
The real enemys are the friends you make a long. 10/10 would get killed by friendly fire again.

[h1] 评测更新时间：2025.06.06 [/h1] --------------------------------------------------------- [h2] （2023.09.25首评） [/h2] --------------------------------------------------------- 以目前的游玩体验来讲，这个游戏的玩法就是背板和寻找当前版本的最佳通关公式，以及更多的背板，[strike] 喜欢受苦类游戏的玩家也许会更喜欢这个游戏。 [/strike] 觉得本文太长的可直接看末尾结论。 游戏的初始人物数值给的太低了，导致在后期关卡里面一旦出现轻微的失误那么就会面临被怪物秒倒的地步。 想提高通关率，那就只能靠刷点数来升级必要的长效技能，例如减伤以及增加血量上限来提升生存率，从而提高每一次游玩的通关几率，[strike] 当然，也要看roll出来的技能好不好，这也是受苦的乐趣所在（bushi [/strike] 武器的词条和roll点方面，这个就是肉眼可见的不平衡了，火器大爹，灵能提鞋，摸鱼仿生，乐子研究，几乎每一次的游玩选择都会偏向于火器，如果有不选火器的情况，那就是所有火器的词条都太差了，又或是玩腻了火器想换个口味。 最近的更新也有平衡过武器词条与数值方面的动作，但可惜没加强到需要的地方上， 举个例子：研究型武器里面的转管机枪，蓄力开火，射速快，弹容量高是它的特性，而蓄力开火这一要素就决定了它是一把团队型武器， 但使用过它的玩家就会马上发现它的短板：预热时间太长被怪物冲脸了，开火时的移速和输出太低被怪物围殴了，甚至是在蓄力完成后，队友就已经把怪物打完了，完全没办法在它应有的场合里发挥它应有的作用， 这就导致了这把武器的上手门槛非常高，以至于大家都更喜欢用简单粗暴的火器型武器，而不是去拿转管机枪去体验拔剑四顾心茫然的感觉。 而且转管机枪居然需要火器类的突触来提升它的使用体验，这就又导致了在当局游玩的突触选择方面，玩家是需要选择研究相关的技能去触发它的词条特性，还是选择选择火器的突触去提升它的DPS， 但很明显，这把武器并没有能够完全改变武器使用体验的词条，所以大多数人都会去选择更多的火器卡牌来增加它的伤害，如果是这样，那么为什么一开始就不去玩火器武器？该武器的物理伤害转换为灵能伤害的词条亦是同理，他们都需要研究类突触以外的突触来改善使用体验。这不只是数值的问题了，这是武器的使用机制与武器本身的定位问题，希望开发者能够重新研究每个种类的突触与相关的词条之间的关联性，而不是单纯地加强或是削弱某些武器的数值以及改变突触技能的强度，不然大家都抱死一种武器来进行游戏了。 联机体验这个挺难说的，我个人是十有九掉，还有一次打不过，也不清楚是我运气太差还是说联机系统本身就有问题，看后续优化吧。 太长不看省流版：未来可期。 --------------------------------------------------------- [h2] （2025.03.26更新） [/h2] --------------------------------------------------------- 《不只是名字改了》 制作团队在酝酿了许久之后，终于拿出了他们的诚意之作。 首先是复杂且极度不平衡的武器系统重构， 现在的武器强化方向也已经精简为单发与连发这两种类型，再也不像以前那么五花八门且华而不实了， 游戏内的各种武器数值与机制在经过调整后，就再也没有所谓的白板数值怪了。 不仅是强势的武器削弱，弱势的武器也得到了加强， 武器的搭配方面也有了更多的选择，甚至还能搭配不同角色自身所携带的buff。 “红”就是最简单粗暴的玻璃大炮， 没什么怪物能在DPS拉满的情况下活下来，如果有，那要么就是boss单位，要么就是你的卡和词条roll的不好。 如果想玩近战秀身法的路子，那就要去玩玩“柳叶刀”了， 游戏更新了许多的近战武器，且拥有了大幅的加强，在有了近战相关的卡牌的加持后，“一刀入星界”的含金量就变得非常高了，而且角色自带高暴击高爆伤的buff，这也让“柳叶刀”能够更好地适应各种单发和连发的武器。 但“柳叶刀”也存在着一个问题，你必须要保证你的角色不处于恐慌状态下才能使用技能进入“星界”状态（也就是无敌状态），而且游戏内也要经常在黑暗的环境下作战，在没有任何光源的情况下，角色的恐惧值将会一直都处于临界水平。 受限于这些，“柳叶刀”的生存能力并没有想象中的那么高，并且开发者也没有在游戏内提到过这一点，但最要命的，还是使用技能时的动作衔接并不是特别流畅，如果能在出刀出伤害的瞬间通过翻滚来取消动作后摇的话，那使用“柳叶刀”的实际游戏体验会进一步上升。 综上所述，“柳叶刀”适合有一定游戏熟练度的玩家，但由于恐惧时不能进入“星界“状态，所以实际游戏体验不会比“红”来的舒服。 “童子军”的buff定位就是坦克，一个纯粹的综合型坦克，最招牌的招式就是先手乱扫一通吸引全场怪物的注意力，然后砸地丢出诱饵后嘎嘎输出，但使用技能的时候是会被控制打断的，而且技能使用的前后摇非常长，在获得“战术撤退”的卡牌后就更长了，且全程不处于无敌状态，这使得“童子军”在使用技能的时候要多过一下脑子，这是我觉得略微不好的地方，既然要爽那就让玩家爽嘛。 “烧杯”给我的印象就是赖皮，在单人模式缺乏回血手段的现版本，“烧杯”自带范围性回血的这一技能，让“烧杯”彻底变成了爹一般的存在，而且最大恐惧值的特性也并不算是完全的debuff属性，因为这个游戏里面还有一张最为强力的卡牌：恐惧状态时增加100%攻击力，但凡抽到这张卡牌，那整局的游戏体验就会开始有质的改变，你会恨不得自己的身上常驻有恐惧状态。 综上所述：只有“童子军”受伤的世界达成了 --------------------------------------------------------- [h2] （2025.06.06更新，已经在最高难度下通关单人+团队咯） [/h2] --------------------------------------------------------- 这次新增了两个boss单位：阿国夫人和拿非利人。 先来说说后室boss的阿国夫人吧，这并不是特别难的boss，各种机制也能够在同一张地图里面见到过，属于是非常容易初见通的boss单位，比外骨骼那血牛硬茬好打多了，但整体的艺术风格实属阴间，毕竟是后室嘛。 [spoiler] 改一改魔偶的巡逻路线吧！每次遇到这家伙都要被迫交几格血当路费！在我躲进柜子之后这家伙就会回到我的行进路线上，我出柜子了就堵我的路，最关键是我还不能绕着走！ [/spoiler] 然后是当局的关底boss：多看一眼就会爆炸的拿非利人 [spoiler] 会电眼逼人的四手霸王（bushi） [/spoiler] 作为关底boss来说，容易被初见杀，但只要肯多花点时间把它招式全部套出来，那打起来可就太简单了。 再说说各种游玩体验： 我个人认为，现版本的轮椅配装是柳叶刀+光子炮+电弧炮，而两把武器也是柳叶刀的专属武器。 首先是光子炮那极致对单的数值面板，在加上追踪的词条后，就是一把通杀任何精英单位和boss的武器，要射程有射程，要输出有输出，而且还能刷个反弹碎片词条来弥补对群能力，也可以刷个追踪词条来增加容错率。 其次是电弧炮，那更是自游戏重制以来就一直存在的对群大爹，这次更新配件还追加了增幅器和光束分离器这俩极致对群的词条，在roll出移速相关的突触后，那这局直接就爽“飞”了（字面意思） 但这俩武器有个最大的毛病，那就是有着蓄力攻击的原因，导致没法很好的应对突发情况。 [spoiler] （你一定很喜欢蒙脸冲刺哥吧？） [/spoiler] 而这就是为什么我强推用柳叶刀来搭配这两把武器的原因： 自从柳叶刀能在恐惧状态下进入星界状态后，就能够很好的驾驭这种带了就会降低生存能力的武器了，极致的武器白板加上高生存容错的角色技能机制形成了极致的互补效应，在玩家有了一定的游戏理解后，这就是最轮椅的通关答案。 最后再给制作组说一句，除非你往后要做PVP，不然就别讲平衡，在玩家积累了游戏机制的理解后，用任何武器和任何角色都能打出很好的效果才是这个游戏的爽点。往后也可以收集一下角色和武器的出场率，以及各种通关的搭配，把这些放出来给大家讨论一下，这也是个调研改进方向的好法子。 [spoiler] 所以我的连发大狙呢？就这么没了？ [/spoiler]

After 40 hours of playtime both solo and coop and going through all the versions of the game (played when it was still Blackout Protocol), I think I finally realized why I am personally so unhappy with this game. The game feels massively unfair. I understand that with roguelite games, death is expected and is part of the core gameplay loop. I've played Hades, Dead Cells, Gatekeeper. The thing is, whenever I die in those games, I could see why I died. I understand why my skill level came up short and I kind of have an idea of what to do better. I realize "okay, I should dodge faster" or "I should watch out for that attack" or "I shouldn't overextend". In this game, every time I die, I don't have any idea how to do it better because this isn't a shooting skill game. It's a "how many times can you dodge before you make a mistake and end your run". There is nothing to learn. There is nothing to think about on the next run. Every time I get a little bit further in my runs, it's not because I played better. It's because the enemies spawned differently or behaved differently. There were't ravagers in the mix. Or the room was a bit bigger, giving more maneuvering room. Or the zombies didn't all rush in at once. Or I got a good perk. Or I got a good tactical grenade. It is NEVER because I feel like I felt like I played better. So, every time I play, I never have a reliable idea of how far I'm going to get because I am at the mercy of randomness and I feel like no amount of skill can overcome that. That is why it feels unfair. The first few versions of the game was a good coop came where it felt like you and your friends were truly battling hordes of monsters, covering for each other but, with every new version and new patch, it felt like they were slowly scraping away a lot of good mechanics or bonuses and locking them behind upgrades that you could only purchase with data nuggets you collect each run. It felt like they deliberately handicapped players from the beginning in an effort to pad gameplay time. People keep saying that it's a roguelite and that I need to give it a few more runs for it to be fun but that defeats the entire point. A roguelite keeps you hooked AFTER each death. In a good roguelite, death is frustrating but also exciting because you want to go AGAIN. Every time I die in this game, I close it because every death has always felt bad and leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

First off: Blackout Protocol is not a bad game. It is however not recommendable at this point of the development. So, Blackout Protocol is a korean twin-stick shooter with rogue-lite elements. You level up your character during your play, acquire new weapons, gain perks, and then use nugs (a form of currency) to purchase definitive passive skills. I did encounter a few bugs during play, such as enemies being stuck, the floor disappearing or a prompt not proceeding further. Nothing game-breaking for the most part, and to be honest, that's not my issue with the game. No, my main issue is that one of the enemies can only be killed during its panic. How do you inflict panic, you may ask? By using psionic weapons, which for the most part, are absolutely underpowered. The only good contender is the Photon Cannon but it's not made to deal with hordes. It's a boss killer. This means that you have to split your perks into both psionic weapons [i]and[/i] something else. Which leads us into another problem: [b]the ammo pool is way too low[/b]. Even with the ammo upgrades, you will struggle to get from one objective to the other if you only rely on one weapon. Ideally, you'd use 2 weapons from the firearms category, but you cannot since you have to deal with the "mandatory psionic damage miniboss". Also, do you fancy playing in co-op? Then get ready for a frustrating experience. The ammo will still be as scarce as it was, but the enemies also receive a massive buff to both their HP and damage, even with only two players. Which only makes the aforementioned problems even worse. As if that wasn't enough, the credits that you need to re-roll perks or purchase new weapons / perks are not shared. Play with someone using a minigun or the flamethrower? Yep, no credits for you! Last but not least: although there are different configurations for the maps (I think two, but there might be a third), you end up always replaying the same maps, with the very same objectives and 0 variability. Since there are no other campaigns and you can't choose maps, you are cursed to forever play the same thing over and over. Which makes the game repetitive and as such quickly boring. In a world where the free Alien Swarm: Reactive Drop exists, there is no way I'm recommending Blackout Protocol. Now, it's still in Early Access and since the gameplay itself is good I might reconsider my review later, but that's it for now.

Changes to the game haven't improved it much in certain ways. Limited number of guns, limited number of per-run upgrades which are gated behind arbitrary "coupons", despite the game still telling you that you can upgrade weapons with credits. The upgrades usually have downsides that make it generally a net negative to take anything. Most guns are basically unusable solo because the reload speed is abysmal while forcing you to walk at a geriatric pace, and reloading is cancelled by every action you perform. This combined with the game's difficulty revolving around locking you in small rooms with near endless amounts of enemies that are faster than you until you kill one specific enemy or survive x number of waves, means that once you run out of ammo in your main gun, your only chance to reload is to eat 2-3 hits with no way to counter it because your melee attack cancels the reload, and rolling also cancels the reload. Using any gun like the sniper rifle, minigun, flamethrower, etc., is basically impossible solo, forcing you to use your flaccid handgun for the bulk of the encounter. Certain guns will also carry an innate movement speed penalty while holding it. The sniper rifle fires comically slow, and stops you from reloading between shots while also reducing your movement speed to nothing, even when you let go of the buttons, until the firing animation is complete. This animation takes ~1.5 seconds to finish, and the reload itself takes ~3 seconds to finish. The minigun takes ~2 seconds to spool before firing, and the reload takes ~4 seconds. You can preemptively begin the spooling process by holding right mouse (which slows you down), but this still means that after spending 4 seconds to reload (while eating ♥♥♥♥ because you can't dodge or melee while reloading), you need to spend another 2 seconds spooling (while eating ♥♥♥♥ because you move slower than everything in the game) before you can start firing again. It feels like reloading and firing sets your movement speed to a specific value, so movement speed increases also feel pointless because you're almost always reloading or firing. All this combined ends up making guns like the assault rifle and submachine gun your only options after a certain point when playing solo, because everything else is gated by actually being able to reload within the small gaps you can get before the enemies are back on top of you.

this game is a huge downgrade at present than when it was still called blackout protocol. back then you could have fun and meaningful progression with a decent amount of challenge, now i have no idea what to make of any of the items. additionally, the psionic energy element and will / fear system being nuked is a very odd choice. that made the enemies, weapons and abilities make sense. without it we're what? operators? the tutorial makes little sense unless you knew the former premise. also, calculators throwing grenades, in a confined space at the first instant they are introduced as a threat is BRAINDEAD design. the barrier locks behind you and you're forced to take a grenade to the face. what the hell. who play-tested this? dead mice? ever heard of 'controlled introduction to players' & the whole idea that enemies should be shown to players in a way they can quickly understand what they do and how to defeat them in a scenario where the player is at an equal or greater advantage. without that its just "oh haha u didn't see the grenade enemy you have no idea about that we added at some random point without any mention at all, u died. uwu too bad!!!" it just feels disjointed and confusing. and yes, what i'm complaining about is what they've done, in the most irritating way possible. i cannot fathom how in the seventh circle of hell you'd want to keep playing this in a team of 4 when we all wipe after being heavily trauma damaged by the first horde, there's no early game way to remove it. so if you get an unlucky instakill tick by a brute, its nuke the run and start over????? maddening. honestly i loved this when i played it as blackout protocol but now it just feels so much worse and i don't really want to waste my time learning something that's just assuming you know what all the changes are. that's bad game design. and no, i'm not interested in grinding it to 'git gud' i should be able to have fun out of the box fully aware its going to be challenging, making it hard for the sake of difficulty is stupid and completely loses the essence as to why people liked it in earlier builds. it just seems like another victim of development creep.

这个游戏怎么说呢，我应该是最早一批玩家吧，从这款游戏在Steam肉鸽游戏节上放出的试玩版开始玩起，三人联机模式很有创意，当时发现有误伤系统，走位什么的还是要考虑的，并不是无脑突突突。 上手游戏难度相当高，敢说一开始自己solo的时候连第二关都到不了吗？（第一次看到后面的关卡还是靠多人游戏）每次都卡断电恢复那里，只能靠不停解锁技能+提高操作来解锁关卡。后来解锁技能越来越多，solo的游戏难度也显著下降，总的来说这个游戏的肉鸽属性还是很强的，上手难度（初期游戏版本）不是一般的高。这个游戏一开始武器是分大类的，物理、灵能、科技、生物对应红、紫、黄、绿四个颜色，你要吃足够多的对应颜色的突触强化才能解锁武器属性，所以当年联机时，大家都会避免选择同一颜色，以免吃不够突触魔方导致武器性能不足，休息室一般会有对应颜色的两个魔方，大家会提前说好颜色避免争抢。早期枪械的属性一开局就随机，所以大家为了随到想要的属性都会频繁重开，我觉得现在的机制（休息室枪械改装台凭券改装）还是很好的，不想要的属性可以花钱洗掉，当然还是要看脸，不过不至于随不到就重开。 对于现在游戏机制的槽点，我觉得取消颜色分类算一个，所有的突触有的堪称神器，有的无限鸡肋，像是为了增加随机效果而增加。以前的四种颜色武器各有特色，需要吃够对应颜色的魔方来解锁性能，武器流派玩法还是很浓的。比如初上手大家多会选择物理系，或者科技系，这两种混搭也行反正吃物理伤害加成，玩到后来会发现其实灵能武器更强。我个人喜欢改版前的灵能武器，因为怪物以前也有紫色的恐惧条，你把他们的恐惧条打空他们会眩晕的，相当于群体控场，关键是连boss也吃这种控场。当时关底（坩埚）boss用灵能散弹枪我能晕到死，而且伤害极为可观（紫色突触吃一个增加10%灵能伤害，还有个好像叫E.M.P的直接增加100%灵能伤害），比物理系武器的后期伤害高多了，我因为灵能系武器的这个特点玩了好久，也无数次通关。以前那种把突触从白金->黄金->白银的分类感觉很好，一目了然，希望恢复下，现在的分类逻辑，白金里面也有鸡肋的，普通的里面反而有效果不俗的，对新手不是很直观。比如我因为还是喜欢用短管霰弹枪，持续火力很关键，我就喜欢近战武器杀死目标秒换膛那个骨骸收集者突触，但是近战武器有耐久度，所以有时得搭配个佐德符文实现近战武器无限耐久，再配上翻滚25%换膛的白金符文，外加3-4弹夹容量改装，有点遇神杀神的架势，谁用谁知道（只是你得养成频繁捡弹药的习惯）。 另外有些枪械的改装，就如其他玩家反映的，有十分鸡肋的，建议继续打磨完善，突出不同武器的差异增加可玩性。但是也有很逆天的，还是用短管霰弹枪做例子，你改装出额外射出0-4发射弹不消耗弹药，再加那个瞄准射击发射独头弹，后期一发独头弹暴击伤害能上千（比狙击枪还狙击枪，让我想起了金枪客），关键还能一秒清空弹夹，boss都哗哗掉血。而原本应该成为特色武器的左轮手枪，后期改装提升的空间却不大，虽然后期单发伤害也不低，但是比起霰弹枪这种可点杀，可瞬间群攻“清场”的武器，就大大逊色了。 最后，关于不同角色的差异，我觉得以前那种不同角色对应颜色属性的路子其实挺不错，现在的修改有点同质化，不过还能接受。只是强烈建议恢复大招的选项功能（以前办公室那关有魔镜，可以换大招，一个人三种大招可选，增加不同流派的玩法），不知道这么好的创意为啥没了？就算是大招与大招之间有点不平衡，可以调整嘛，没必要一刀切。还有，关卡有随机属性，但是还不够，多次游戏后路线基本都是二选一，或者小的随机效果（后半程基本没有大的地图随机性），长期游戏性不足。另外讲一下游戏里的“后室“隐藏关其实不错，算是给游戏增加变数和额外游戏性了，只是后室刷的地方太固定了，难免会有为了刷到”后室“入口而反复尝试的可能，长期来看不一定是好事，或许可以尝试更隐蔽的进入方式？鼓励玩家去进行环境探索和互动，这样进入后室才有惊喜和挑战性。 总的来说，我作为这款游戏的元老玩家，我是很看好游戏的创意的。每次版本玩腻了，放几个月有了版本更新后还是有兴趣一战的。希望这款游戏的更新能跟上，内容扩展能持续进行中。给差评的朋友（很多游戏时间甚至是个位数的），这款游戏可能不如你想象得那么快餐，比起有些上手就能”爽“的动作游戏，这个游戏需要一点循序渐进和积累，所以可以先沉下心多玩几个小时再来评价。

It's very bland and unforgiving, a pretty poor combo to try and entice someone into playing it. The game seems poorly balanced for solo and focused on multiplayer, in which case why even make a solo mode? Reading the other reviews seems like the game was a lot more in the past which puts me off even more after playing it. You get locked in a room often, with little room to move and body blocked in by enemies. No way to get out because the dodge doesn't go through them, just a mediocre melee attack that relies on RNG weapon drops. The 'fear' mechanic ends up being perpetual because the afformentioned locked rooms are also in the dark with no way to light it up without an unlockable portable light that relies on RNG drops and takes up your grenade slot - which seems to be the primary way to deal with hordes. So you die from a horde you can't aoe down or you die from a horde that catches you easily when the fear mechanic kicks in. Also enemies can dive at you from behind walls, which due to the poor camera positioning and lack of x-ray effect to mitigate foreground items is completely unavoidable. Shame because it looks nice visually and the basic gunplay is good, but that's all there is - really basic gunplay. Avoid.

Overall, I really enjoy the game as a twin-stick shooter. The gameplay feels incredibly responsive, and the combat loop is genuinely satisfying. From a pure mechanics standpoint, the developers nailed the "feel" of the action. The biggest disappointment for me is the multiplayer. I bought this game specifically for the co-op experience, but several design choices make it hard to enjoy: Scaling Issues: As soon as you set a run to "Public," the difficulty spikes—even if no one has joined yet. This makes hosting a game feel like a punishment rather than an invitation. There would likely be a much larger online player base if the difficulty would not change or only scaled based on the actual number of players in the session. Lack of Story Progression: Why does co-op halt story progress? I’ve tried to join friends, but they often refuse because they want to actually move the plot forward. It feels like the game is actively discouraging you from playing together. Another thing I did not like that certain menus (like the Weapon Perk window) cannot be closed quickly during combat. In a fast-paced shooter like this, every single pop-up window should be closeable instantly with the Esc key. Losing a run because you're stuck looking at a menu while being hit is incredibly frustrating.

Definitely feels like some of the negative reviews for this game are either frankly just... not gamers.. or played a different version entirely. The feeling of guns and gun upgrades is great, and the alternative paths you can unlock, and alternative layouts makes the replays when you wipe very fun too, even at full price this games well worth it for co-op. On sale it's a must have if you've a group. The game lacks a little bit solo, but it's still very fun for a solo twinstick adventure.

Section 13 is a roguelite twin-stick shooter developed by Ocean Drive Studio, Inc. and published by Ocean Drive Studio, Inc. together with Kakao Games. Combining science fiction action with paranormal horror and cooperative gameplay systems, the game creates an experience built around dangerous expeditions, escalating threats, and persistent progression. It takes familiar roguelite foundations and strengthens them through a setting filled with corporate secrecy, mysterious experiments, and unpredictable supernatural danger. The story unfolds inside a heavily secured underground facility owned by S2P Corporation, a shadowy organization responsible for researching and containing dangerous anomalies. Disaster strikes when a severe containment failure unleashes chaos deep within one of the company's classified locations. Strange creatures escape confinement, systems collapse, and the situation quickly spirals beyond control. To address the crisis, a group of specialized agents is deployed into the facility to uncover what happened and contain the growing threat before conditions deteriorate even further. Players take control of operatives with distinct personalities and backgrounds, adding narrative flavor to the action-heavy structure. As missions progress, fragments of information slowly reveal more about both the facility and the characters navigating its dangers. While storytelling does not dominate the experience, it provides enough mystery to strengthen player investment and gives purpose to repeated runs through hostile environments. Combat serves as the foundation of the gameplay experience. Movement remains fast and responsive, requiring players to constantly reposition while handling aggressive enemy encounters. Combat arenas quickly become chaotic as enemy pressure increases, forcing careful management of ammunition, mobility, and tactical awareness. Success rarely comes from standing still or relying entirely on raw firepower. Survival depends on balancing offense and defense while adapting to constantly changing battlefield conditions. The roguelite structure gives long-term progression meaningful depth. Every failed attempt contributes toward future improvement through unlockable upgrades, equipment enhancements, and new combat options. Rather than punishing defeat completely, the game uses failure as part of advancement. Each run teaches players more about enemy behavior while gradually expanding available tools and tactical possibilities. This progression loop creates a satisfying sense of growth that encourages players to continue pushing deeper into dangerous territory. Customization also contributes heavily to replay value. Weapons, upgrades, and progression systems allow players to shape different approaches to combat depending on preferred playstyle. Some builds may emphasize survivability and control while others focus on aggressive damage output. Experimentation becomes an important part of long-term enjoyment because systems interact in ways that reward adaptation rather than forcing identical strategies every run. One of Section 13's more interesting mechanics revolves around psychological pressure. Missions are not only dangerous because of enemies and environmental hazards. Mental strain becomes another obstacle players must manage during high-pressure situations. Rising fear levels introduce additional complications that can directly interfere with performance, reinforcing the paranormal atmosphere while creating another layer of strategic decision-making. This system helps separate Section 13 from more traditional action roguelites by making emotional control part of survival itself. The setting further strengthens the experience. Underground laboratories filled with failed experiments, corporate secrets, and hostile anomalies create a strong sense of mystery and danger throughout progression. The facility itself feels hostile and unstable, reinforcing tension even during quieter moments between combat encounters. Environmental design supports both science fiction themes and horror influences without overwhelming the core action focus. Cooperative gameplay elevates much of the experience further. Teams can coordinate movement, support each other during difficult encounters, and overcome escalating threats through communication and teamwork. Cooperative play naturally enhances replayability because group dynamics constantly change how missions unfold. Optional friendly-fire settings add another variable for players seeking additional challenge or unpredictability. Visually, Section 13 emphasizes clarity and atmosphere over excessive visual complexity. The top-down perspective keeps combat readable even during chaotic encounters involving large enemy groups and environmental hazards. Enemy designs reinforce the unsettling corporate-horror atmosphere, while lighting and environmental details help establish a facility that feels both technologically advanced and deeply unsafe. The game does carry limitations common to the roguelite genre. Progression naturally involves repetition, and players unfamiliar with repeated run structures may find early difficulty demanding. Solo players may also encounter tougher moments compared to coordinated multiplayer groups. However, those challenges feel intentional rather than unfair and contribute to the sense of long-term mastery the game encourages. Section 13 succeeds because it combines action, progression systems, cooperative design, and atmospheric storytelling into a package that remains engaging across repeated play sessions. Ocean Drive Studio delivers a roguelite shooter that understands the value of both immediate combat satisfaction and meaningful long-term growth. Its combination of tension, customization, mystery, and cooperative depth creates a memorable experience for players looking for fast-paced action with layers of progression beneath the surface. Rating: 7/10

I want to like this game, and I guess I will have to since I am over the 2hr limit to return. But there is a LOT of artificial difficulty added onto the game. For example to make it more "challenging" you have to stick to lighted areas, if you don't you build up a fear meter that if filled will cause the camera to zoom in, screen distortion effects will start, and you take extra damage from enemies. The problem is that "event rooms" where you have to survive a horde frequently take place in dark areas. Which then highlights the next few issues. Very frequently you are limited to small rooms with red barriers that you can't cross but enemies can. Very early on you will see this in the lobby area where you are stuck in a small room while enemies rush it from the outside. The only reason this area is frustrating is because, again, red barriers confine you to a small area and restrict your movement, oh and yeah in the dark too for extra punishment. I say you will see this area frequently since the maps are also static. There are apparently a handful of maps that they use of each area since the very first level changed once I found the second agent to be a little different. Each run will be on the same maps though you can find passcodes for "short cuts" randomly. That's really all the changes that happen, it's random where items are and what modifiers you get along the way. Which brings me to the final issue. The weapon selection is....limited. There is space for more but after a year I don't think we are going to see more guns anytime soon. There is also a noticeable delay of several seconds to actually begin firing for several of them as well. So it's obvious these weapons were designed with co-op in mind...and solo play is just not there. Especially since aiming so you make your hits count slows your movement to a crawl. The photon cannon for example hits hard but takes about 2 seconds to charge before actually firing, and reloading is cancelled by any actions. Melee, dodging, swapping guns, everything cancels reload which depending on the weapon may make you rely on melee...and that becomes an issue because enemies will swarm you and beat you to death before you even inconvenience the most basic enemy with a melee attack. This makes the shotgun ironically one of the best weapons purely on the fact it's individual shell loading. Usually an annoyance in other games, but actually very powerful an ability here. Finally the upgrades. Mid run you can do body upgrades that usually come with a hefty downside. Want 10% recoil control? Well it can come with an extra 20% damage taken. This means you usually with two options that suck and you can't reroll; and if you try to just cancel altogether you just basically waste the upgrade for no benefit like coins or health. With weapons you get a similar issue but in the opposite direction. You get WAY more options for weapons than you can possibly add onto them, my shotgun already has 12 options I can possibly roll...but you can only slot 4 in a run. That's it. Between runs you can upgrade all agents, but that comes with the issue that every upgrade very piecemeal. Overall this almost feels like it was a game designed to be a mobile game but then shifted to PC development at some point. Some of these design choices maybe would make sense in that context. What's worse is at times you can see an interesting game under it all but the constant restrictions means the game gets in it's own way to be enjoyable. I got this on a deep deep sale and honestly I still feel I kinda overpaid for the experience.

The good: Cute characters. Doesn't do anything offensively bad. The bad: Technical issues. Lacks thematic depth. Lacks polish. Doesn't randomize it's level layout. The verdict: Pretty cute. Not great, not terrible, but way overpriced for what it is. I wish they'd polish out some of the most glaring technical issues and actually flesh out the lore in a way that isn't just copying better games and presuming people will recognize it. As it stands, they just slapped an "SCP" sticker on a twin-stick shooter and called it a day. The redirect: Control, Neon Chrome, Abiotic Factor.

I can understand where some of the hate is coming from. Honestly if it hadn't been 75% off I doubt I would have picked it up. But for a $20 game it feels pretty shallow. The gameplay is fairly smooth, although it's a bit janky using ranged weapons on stairs. Some of the terrain models are a bit "Sticky" so moving around objects while in a fight can be kind of tough. The learning curve isn't too bad and the unlocks are pretty generous so after a few runs you'll have made some good progress. Unfortunately, this game suffers from the same problem that I feel a lot of rogue-lites do and that is balance... This was my progression through the game... 1st Run - Starter Assault Rifle (Not Bad), Starter Pistol (BAD!) 2nd Run - Bought a Pump Shotgun (Just...Okay) 3rd Run - Sniper Rifle (Decent)... put a suppressor on it (Very Good) 4th Run - Bought an upgrade to run both Sniper Rifle and Assault Rifle... set a new PB (First Boss/room #4) 5th Run - Bought a Sub Machine Gun (Great)... found out that it has a heal mod and a half second reload (Broken AF!) game turned into easy mode and cleared the run without any real challenge. So TL;DR... If you can get the game for 5 or 10 bucks, it's worth it and after your first run unlock the Sub Machine Gun for easy mode.

The gameplay loop for what it is , is fun enough. The story is interesting. I just dislike that some of the events is held in areas that is reliant to have [spoiler]your max fear upgraded or to have the grenade that lights up the place[/spoiler]. Another annoyance is that due to the isometric angle, some of the environmental clutter fully hides the enemies until you accidentally bump into them. Speaking of environmental clutter, you can get stuck on the smallest bit that you cant even see!! The voice acting btw is subpar. very reminiscent of "that" certain quality of English dubbed anime so it's hard to feel sympathetic to some of the voiced parts of the ingame files lmao. Also as someone who enjoys roguelike, this game gets boring to play alone after a few runs. definitely feels like it is made leaning more on co-op play for it to be fun. Defo a game to buy when it's heavily on sale.

It's a roguelike where you run and gun through a variety of levels. It's not particularly innovative though, and the player-base is dead. It's 5 dollars, so you're definitely getting what you pay for... The game really survives on it's run and gun mechanics. You, periodically, will pick up modifiers that make you better in a spec area whether it's weapon charge or reload or damage output etc. It's all very bog standard roguelike, but this game has issues: High level gameplay ultimately comes down to reload time. That's it. The more shots you can put downrange the better you'll typically do, and that means keeping your weapon firing more than anything. What tends to happen is you have a really fast awesome weapon that takes forever to reload and the zombies come in faster than you can reload the weapon so you die. This is a huge problem for the higher levels where a sniper rifle can output 200+ damage a shot, but be utterly worthless for clearing mobs, which is the most important aspect of the gameplay. The slower the reload, generally, the more dead you are. That kind of sucks because that means the SMG is the only viable gun at a high level. That's your option...an SMG. You will never be able to get a low enough reload time out of a gatling to make it useful. It really comes down to that. The sniper doesn't fire fast enough and the reload is atrocious. All this being said, that means the first character you get, "Red" ends up being the most viable at a high level because of her reload ability. That brings me to my next point: Each character has a separate ability, but they're all pretty forgettable unless you're really spec'ing for them. One character can push enemies away, one can heal, one does more damage output modifier and slight invulnerability, which ends up being pretty useless, and one can reload faster. Each character has a fairly forgettable story, and a couple of the characters are overtly evil. The fortnite style art direction and cutesy characters don't really convey how comically evil you're set up to be. You're definitely not playing 'the good guys' in this story. Having played it for a few hours I felt like it was a rather weak experience overall. It needs some serious balance and a few weapons passes to make something besides the SMG worthwhile. Overall: It's fairly bland, mildly enjoyable, and at least cheap for what it is. If you're curious pick it up while it's on sale.

For context, I used hacks such as removing skill cool-downs and increasing in-run currency when I played, and I would not have kept playing if I had not, because I played it solo. The game may be too hard for a single player. I finished my first run ever using Beaker, the female chemist, because she had an AoE, heal-over-time skill. I'm placing this first because this game was balanced for co-op, with a difficulty option, and the base difficulty is almost an easy mode, where one doesn't even have to consider ammo consumption. And after you beat a run on a difficulty level, you can set it to the next difficulty and so on until level 3, which is the last and has achievements tied to it. Where the game excels is that it feels good to play, but again, there needs to be a serious balance pass in solo play. Certain weapons such as the minigun are nigh-useless, the ramp up time is what holds it back, until you get addons (they drop from harder enemies), which allows you to craft a build; and that gets to issues most rogue-likes have such as not getting the exact addons you need to make the build you want in the run; and btw, how do you know if a build is good for a given weapon? Well, you don't, and that's a problem. There's no way to test weapons you have; for example, as a solo player, the mini gun is near pointless because the time to fire (called weapon charge time) and reload time is too high, and your character slows down as you turn. But if you manage to get addons that fix the first two and a special one that makes your bullets home in on the target within 7 m, then the minigun feels much better. But how would you even know that? There's no way to test the weapons with addons attached. The bottom line is that the game feels good to play, and right now it's on sale for 5.00 USD. Are there better top-down shooters? Probably, but I haven't played any yet with a feel as good as this game. If you get it for $5 USD at its current sale price, I'm confident you'll get your money's worth if you're willing to deal with the issues I listed above. Very pleasant co-op top down shooter. Controls feel tight and responsive (that's a problem for about half the games in this genre). Up to 3 players in a game, still not too hard to play solo. Gameplay wise, the biggest hurdle is the general lack of reliable healing except one gun (the SMG) that has a healing weapon perk. This limits build variety since NOT taking the SMG for healing as one of your two guns kneecaps you. The characters and humor in the story also click with me. Story bits unlock with tokens gained during the missions, but you play the dialogues or read the data files between the missions so there's no time pressure or anybody waiting on you to absorb it. I haven't run into any bugs. If you have very high ping to the host (250+) then multiplayer gets real annoying; you can roll away from an attack (gives I-frames) but get hit anyway while your dead body still lands at the end of your roll. Lowish ping and that's not a problem. There's also one spot - the lab with fire vortices turned on - where it gets framey (but still playable). Besides that one spot, I've no other performance issues - buttery smooth. I think $20 is a pretty fair price for this. I got it on sale for $5 and I've definitely gotten MORE than I paid for.

I've been trying to find games like Alienation on the ps4 and nothing that I've played on PC hit those marks. Section 13 is the closest game I have played so far to that, all in all great top down/twin stick shooter. An aspect that I think that would make this game better are horde modes and weapon upgrade selection. The game focuses on mainly objective type of waves rather than just a random wave/horde spawn intervals. If that was to be added into the current game I think it would take things to the next level. Switching gears over to how weapon systems work in the game, there really isn't a direct upgrade path with a weapon itself. Weapon upgrades are in the form of how random perks work in the game when you select them off of the random black cubes you earn after objectives. IMO, the random perks should be upgrades you can apply to your weapons before you start the match/game (since everything is ran in one playthrough, its like permadeath with upgradeables overtime in the lobby). Yes that may defeat the whole "rogue like" playstyle of game its something that I'd rather prefer. (rogue like twin stick shooters seem to be more and more popular these days and I'd rather have the option to upgrades my weapons). Overall 8.3, top down like game 10/10 what I was looking for, horde spawn type gameplay 4/10 almost too predictable.
